clue.text: Prescription issued with tablets?

parts.note: reads like a doctor's script handed out with pills, but the tablets are the stone ones Moses brought down from Sinai, each carrying a divine rule

explanation.surface: A doctor writes a prescription and hands over a packet of pills.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical picture of a prescription with tablets misleads; a 'prescription' is also a rule laid down, and the Ten were given on two stone tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: A biblical rule laid down by God is a prescription in the sense of an order that must be obeyed.

clue.text: Revealed due to bent?

parts.note: bent is old British slang for gay, so this is someone exposed publicly because of their sexuality

explanation.surface: Something was exposed because it was crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like crooked or corrupt, but it is dated British slang for gay; having one's sexuality made public against one's will is the sense wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exposed publicly as gay without consent is the modern sense of the verb.

clue.text: Confusion of Frenchman over English language point

indicators.note: in a down clue the Frenchman's letter sits over, that is above, the rest

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman
LANG is a common abbreviation of language
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A Frenchman muddles an English grammar point.
explanation.definitionFit: A jumble or mixture of things is a muddle, so a confusion fits.

clue.text: He barely enjoys his free time!

definitions.text: He barely enjoys his free time!

parts.words: He barely enjoys his free time!
parts.note: barely here means wearing nothing at all, so this man spends his leisure hours unclothed

explanation.surface: A man who hardly gets to enjoy his days off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' seems to mean hardly; read literally it means in the bare, naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who spends leisure time without clothes is a naturist.

clue.text: Slaughter of large number over large area

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: a mass is a great quantity
an acre is a sizeable unit of land area

explanation.surface: Killing of many people across a wide region.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiscriminate killing of many people is slaughter.

clue.text: They are useless, pointless, endless

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: needless means unnecessary, serving no purpose

explanation.surface: A grumble that some people are good for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' removes the final S from NEEDLESS; 'They' is the definition, and needles, with their points, play on 'pointless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing or knitting needles are things that can be referred to as they, the pronoun standing for the plural noun.

clue.text: Old flasher seen in the street!

definitions.text: Old flasher seen in the street!

parts.words: Old flasher seen in the street!
parts.note: the flasher is a flashing amber lamp on a pole marking a British pedestrian crossing, in use since the 1930s

explanation.surface: An elderly exhibitionist spotted out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flasher' suggests an indecent man; here it is a flashing light. In Britain an amber globe on a striped pole marks a zebra crossing, named after transport minister Leslie Hore-Belisha.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange globe lamp at a British zebra crossing blinks on and off, making it a street light that flashes.

clue.text: Cherries' outdoor training facility

parts.note: fruit trees such as cherries are trained to grow flat along a lattice or wall outdoors

explanation.surface: An open-air ground where a team nicknamed the Cherries practises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cherries' suggests a sports team (Bournemouth's football club is nicknamed the Cherries), but it means cherry trees being trained flat against a framework.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice or wall framework on which fruit trees are trained to grow flat is a training structure for plants.

clue.text: Hairdresser's perk?

parts.note: a fringe is hair cut over the forehead, so a stylist's bonus playfully gets that name

explanation.surface: An extra the salon offers its staff.
explanation.walkthrough: A perk is a bonus in addition to pay; for a hairdresser it whimsically involves the hair over the brow.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra given to an employee beyond salary, such as a company car, is a perk.

clue.text: Praise former tax? Not labour leader

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: not here asks for the letter that follows to be left out of the tax word

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

indicators.note: the leader of labour is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Applauding a tax that was abolished, though not by the Labour Party's chief.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or glorify someone is to praise them.

clue.text: It delivers if I press end roughly

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely, so the letters of these words are only approximately in order

explanation.surface: A gadget gives something out when I push the end hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that hands out items, like cash or soap, delivers them.

clue.text: Country where a person's embraced by another

indicators.note: being embraced is being held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: another country, here India
one's means a person's

explanation.surface: Somewhere a person is hugged by someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: An archipelago nation in Southeast Asia is a country.

clue.text: Memorise Shakespearean role before noon

indicators.note: before puts the king's name ahead of the abbreviation

parts.note: King Lear is the title role of a Shakespeare tragedy

explanation.surface: An actor must learn the part of Lear before midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To commit to memory is to get by heart, which is to memorise.

clue.text: Hard line Democrat stalled…

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
an edge is a boundary line
D stands for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A hardline Democrat holds up proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade commitment and play for time is to prevaricate, which is close to stalling.

clue.text: Blue feathers fanned out

parts.note: down is soft fine feathers
cast means spread or thrown out, as a net is

explanation.surface: Blue plumage spread out like a peacock's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling dejected or low-spirited.

clue.text: …new electoral system one set in order

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: putting the letters of these words in a fresh order shuffles them

explanation.surface: A fresh voting system, one that has been set up properly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from the previous one with ellipses; 'order' rearranges SET IN into STINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unspoilt and in mint condition is as good as fresh.

clue.text: He may speak Latin, using it in translation

indicators.note: translating turns words into something else, so these letters are converted to a new form

explanation.surface: A man who talks Latin, putting it into English.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled in foreign tongues is a polyglot, able to speak many.

clue.text: Spar? Box, mostly, with energy one's lacking

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: taken as the word itself

indicators.note: the energy word goes without the letter for one

parts.note: spirit means vigour or energy
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is a short is

explanation.surface: A boxer sparring, mostly, though one's tired and lacking energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spar' and 'Box' suggest boxing, but the definition is a ship's pole; BO comes from BOX, and SPRIT is SPIRIT minus I.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole projecting from a sailing ship's bow is a nautical spar.

clue.text: French dish with French water on table

parts.note: plat is French for a dish
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A French dish and a carafe of water are set on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' is not furniture but a tableland, a raised area of flat land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableland, a raised level expanse of high ground, is the geographic sense.

clue.text: Unusual stigma found by church

parts.note: a stigma is a mark or scar
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An odd mark discovered beside the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare or in short supply is uncommon, unusual.

clue.text: Us state taking fifth amendment before state body

indicators.note: before places the first pieces ahead of the verb

parts.note: CA is the postal code for California

indicators.note: the fifth letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: to aver is to state or declare

explanation.surface: A state invokes the Fifth Amendment before a state legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Fifth Amendment' evokes the US right to silence; it actually means the fifth letter of 'amendment', D.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse, especially one used for dissection, is a dead body.

clue.text: Tom will cut you a good deal

definitions.text: Tom will cut you a good deal

parts.words: Tom will cut you a good deal
parts.note: Tom of Mark Twain's novel bears the surname of a person whose job is sawing timber, cutting a lot

explanation.surface: A man named Tom offers you a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut you a good deal' sounds like a bargain; a timber worker cuts a great deal of wood, and Tom is Mark Twain's boy hero.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who saws timber in a sawmill bears this name, as does Twain's Tom.

clue.text: Capital account's credit note

parts.note: AC is short for account; the 's is a short has
A is a musical note

explanation.surface: Money held in an account, with a credit note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks financial alongside account and credit, but it is a city: the capital of Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city of Ghana is its seat of government, a capital.

clue.text: Badly-organised but impressive

indicators.note: badly organised letters are jumbled out of their proper order

explanation.surface: An event that was chaotic but still made a big impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grand, imposing or showy is impressive.

clue.text: Strange, gruesome characters eliminating, say, you and me

indicators.note: strange letters are oddly arranged, so these are mixed up
the letters for you and me are removed from the mixed pool

parts.note: the word taken as written supplies the pool of letters
said aloud, you sounds like the letter U
taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: Weird, grisly figures who are trying to get rid of you and me.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U ('you', said aloud) and ME from GRUESOME and the remaining letters, mixed up by 'Strange', give the monsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant man-eating monsters are fairytale figures, characters in stories.

clue.text: Crude nicety? Sob, perhaps

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so these letters are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: A coarse remark about manners, followed by crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' mixes NICETY and SOB; the whole clue also defines, since S.O.B. (son of a bitch) is an example of a coarse expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude or offensive word, such as S.O.B., is a crude expression.

clue.text: He's rendered by clever divas

indicators.note: rendered by suggests the name is given by the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An opera composer is performed by talented sopranos.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian opera composer of Aida is a man, referred to here simply as he.

clue.text: Express in grand campaign for some tabloids?

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
to press is to campaign or push for something
to utter is to express in words

explanation.surface: The Daily Express runs a big crusade, as some tabloids do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' with its capital looks like the Daily Express, a British tabloid, fitting the surface; it is really the verb meaning to say something. A grand is British slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensationalist popular newspapers are known collectively by this disparaging name.
